025/**
026 * The PaintLauncher class provides functionality for launching and managing
027 * a graphical user interface (GUI) designed to assist users in navigating through
028 * workflow-related applications in the Glyco-PAINT software suite.
029 * <p>
030 * The GUI includes components like buttons, labels, and panels arranged in a specific layout
031 * to represent a workflow. The class utilizes mappings between user-friendly labels
032 * and associated application identifiers, enabling the conditional display of actionable
033 * buttons or visual-only workflow steps based on the map contents.
034 * <p>
035 * Features:
036 * - Customized GUI appearance with consistent sizing, fonts, and colors.
037 * - Creation of customizable buttons and section labels with hover effects and styling.
038 * - Dynamic rendering of workflow paths using arrows and defined visual elements.
039 * - Integration to external application launching using associated identifiers.
040 * - Non-resizable, centered application window with a footer.
041 * <p>
042 * The GUI is intended to provide a user-friendly gateway for interacting
043 * with Glyco-PAINT tools or associated processes.
044 */
045public class PaintLauncher {
046
047    private static final Map<String, String> APP_MAP = new LinkedHashMap<>();
048    private static final String JAR_DIR = "jars";
049
050    static {
051        APP_MAP.put("Get Omero", "paint-get-omero");
052        APP_MAP.put("Create Experiment", "paint-create-experiment");
053        APP_MAP.put("Run TrackMate", null); // visual only
054        APP_MAP.put("Generate Squares", "paint-generate-squares");
055        APP_MAP.put("Viewer", "paint-viewer");
056        APP_MAP.put("Analyse Results", null); // visual only
057    }
058
059
060    /**
061     * Initializes and displays the main graphical user interface (GUI) for the Glyco-PAINT Launcher.
062     * <p>
063     * This method sets up the main window of the application, sized to its contents, featuring
064     * a title, a workflow panel with buttons and visual elements, and a footer. Buttons in the workflow
065     * panel are dynamically created based on the {@code APP_MAP} field, each associated with specific
066     * functionalities or applications. The GUI elements use customized styles, colors, and layouts
067     * optimized for a consistent appearance.
068     * <p>
069     * The window is designed to be non-resizable, centered on the screen, and includes functionality
070     * for launching external applications defined by app mappings.
071     */
072    private static void createAndShowGUI() {
073        JFrame frame = new JFrame("Glyco-PAINT Launcher");
074        frame.setDefaultCloseOperation(JFrame.EXIT_ON_CLOSE);
075        frame.setResizable(false);
076
077        Color bg           = new Color(35, 39, 42);
078        Color fg           = new Color(240, 240, 240);
079        Color accent       = new Color(0x4E9AF1);
080        Color runColor     = new Color(0xBFD7F8);      // "Run TrackMate"
081        Color analyseColor = new Color(0xD8E7FB);  // "Analyse Results"
082        Color arrowMain    = new Color(210, 210, 210);
083        Color arrowShadow  = new Color(80, 80, 80);
084
085        JPanel root = new JPanel(new BorderLayout());
086        root.setBackground(bg);
087        root.setBorder(new EmptyBorder(20, 20, 20, 20));
088
089        JLabel title = new JLabel("Glyco-PAINT Launcher", SwingConstants.CENTER);
090        title.setForeground(fg);
091        title.setFont(new Font("SansSerif", Font.BOLD, 20));
092        title.setBorder(new EmptyBorder(0, 0, 20, 0));
093        root.add(title, BorderLayout.NORTH);
094
095        // Main workflow panel
096        JPanel flowPanel = new JPanel();
097        flowPanel.setLayout(new BoxLayout(flowPanel, BoxLayout.Y_AXIS));
098        flowPanel.setBackground(bg);
099
100        int index = 0;
101        int total = APP_MAP.size();
102        Dimension standardSize = new Dimension(280, 45);
103
104        for (Map.Entry<String, String> entry : APP_MAP.entrySet()) {
105            String label = entry.getKey();
106            String target = entry.getValue();
107
108            JComponent comp;
109            if (target == null) {
110                Color boxColor = "Run TrackMate".equals(label) ? runColor : analyseColor;
111                comp = createSectionLabel(label, boxColor, Color.DARK_GRAY, standardSize);
112            } else {
113                JButton btn = createStyledButton(label, accent, fg, standardSize);
114                btn.addActionListener(e -> launchApp(target, frame));
115                comp = btn;
116            }
117
118            comp.setAlignmentX(Component.CENTER_ALIGNMENT);
119            flowPanel.add(comp);
120
121            if (++index < total) {
122                JLabel arrow = createBoldArrow(arrowMain, arrowShadow);
123                flowPanel.add(arrow);
124            }
125        }
126
127        // Add vertical glue to keep the bottom visible
128        flowPanel.add(Box.createVerticalGlue());
129        root.add(flowPanel, BorderLayout.CENTER);
130
131        JLabel footer = new JLabel("Hans Bakker • © 2025", SwingConstants.CENTER);
132        footer.setForeground(new Color(160, 160, 160));
133        footer.setFont(new Font("SansSerif", Font.PLAIN, 12));
134        footer.setBorder(new EmptyBorder(20, 0, 0, 0));
135        root.add(footer, BorderLayout.SOUTH);
136
137        frame.setContentPane(root);
138
139        // Size the window to its contents rather than a fixed size: the title bar, borders and
140        // fonts differ per system and display scaling (on Windows a fixed 600 px cut off the
141        // last boxes). Keep the original width of at least 420 px.
142        frame.pack();
143        frame.setSize(Math.max(420, frame.getWidth()), frame.getHeight());
144        frame.setLocationRelativeTo(null);
145        frame.setVisible(true);
146    }
147
148    /**
149     * Creates a styled JButton with custom appearance and behavior.
150     * <p>
151     * This method sets properties such as font, colors, size, cursor, and border
152     * to create a visually consistent button. It also adds mouse listeners to
153     * provide a hover effect by adjusting the background color.
154     *
155     * @param text   The text to be displayed on the button.
156     * @param accent The primary accent color for the button (used as the background color).
157     * @param fg     The color for the button's text.
158     * @param size   The dimensions of the button.
159     * @return A JButton instance with the applied styles and behavior.
160     */
161    private static JButton createStyledButton(String text, Color accent, Color fg, Dimension size) {
162        JButton btn = new JButton(text);
163        btn.setPreferredSize(size);
164        btn.setMaximumSize(size);
165        btn.setMinimumSize(size);
166        btn.setFocusPainted(false);
167        btn.setFont(new Font("SansSerif", Font.BOLD, 14));
168        btn.setForeground(fg);
169        btn.setBackground(accent);
170        btn.setBorder(BorderFactory.createEmptyBorder(10, 20, 10, 20));
171        btn.setCursor(Cursor.getPredefinedCursor(Cursor.HAND_CURSOR));
172        btn.setOpaque(true);
173
174        btn.addMouseListener(new MouseAdapter() {
175            @Override
176            public void mouseEntered(MouseEvent e) {
177                btn.setBackground(accent.brighter());
178            }
179
180            @Override
181            public void mouseExited(MouseEvent e) {
182                btn.setBackground(accent);
183            }
184        });
185
186        return btn;
187    }
188
189    /**
190     * Creates a styled JLabel with custom appearance and size. The label is centered
191     * with the specified text, background color, foreground color, and dimensions.
192     *
193     * @param text    The text to be displayed on the label.
194     * @param bgColor The background color of the label.
195     * @param fg      The foreground color (text color) of the label.
196     * @param size    The dimensions of the label (preferred, maximum, and minimum sizes).
197     * @return A JLabel instance with the applied styles and specified properties.
198     */
199    @SuppressWarnings("SameParameterValue")
200    private static JLabel createSectionLabel(String text, Color bgColor, Color fg, Dimension size) {
201        JLabel label = new JLabel(text, SwingConstants.CENTER);
202        label.setOpaque(true);
203        label.setBackground(bgColor);
204        label.setForeground(fg);
205        label.setFont(new Font("SansSerif", Font.BOLD, 14));
206        label.setBorder(BorderFactory.createEmptyBorder(10, 20, 10, 20));
207        label.setPreferredSize(size);
208        label.setMaximumSize(size);
209        label.setMinimumSize(size);
210        return label;
211    }
212
213    /**
214     * Creates a JLabel representing a bold arrow with customized appearance.
215     * <p>
216     * The arrow is displayed as a large, bold, and centered downward arrow ("↓")
217     * with a shadow effect, using the specified main and shadow colors. This method
218     * customizes the label's font, alignment, border, and preferred size.
219     *
220     * @param main   The primary color of the arrow.
221     * @param shadow The color used to create the shadow effect for the arrow.
222     * @return A JLabel instance with a styled bold arrow and shadow effect.
223     */
224    private static JLabel createBoldArrow(Color main, Color shadow) {
225        JLabel arrow = new JLabel("↓", SwingConstants.CENTER) {
226            @Override
227            protected void paintComponent(Graphics g) {
228                Graphics2D g2 = (Graphics2D) g.create();
229                g2.setFont(getFont());
230                FontMetrics fm = g2.getFontMetrics();
231                String s = getText();
232                int x = (getWidth() - fm.stringWidth(s)) / 2;
233                int y = (getHeight() + fm.getAscent()) / 2 - 4;
234
235                // shadow
236                g2.setColor(shadow);
237                g2.drawString(s, x + 1, y + 1);
238                // main arrow
239                g2.setColor(main);
240                g2.drawString(s, x, y);
241                g2.dispose();
242            }
243        };
244        arrow.setFont(new Font("SansSerif", Font.BOLD, 32)); // larger, thicker arrow
245        arrow.setBorder(new EmptyBorder(10, 0, 10, 0));
246        arrow.setAlignmentX(Component.CENTER_ALIGNMENT);
247        arrow.setPreferredSize(new Dimension(300, 35));
248        return arrow;
249    }
250
251    /**
252     * Launches an external application by locating a JAR file with a specified prefix
253     * and executing it as a new process, with the same Java the launcher runs on.
254     * <p>
255     * The JAR is looked for first in the folder that holds the launcher's own JAR (which is
256     * where the bundled Glyco-PAINT app keeps all its JARs), then in {@code jars} under the
257     * current working directory. Displays an error if no matching JAR is found or if the
258     * process fails to start.
259     *
260     * @param jarPrefix The prefix of the JAR file name to be located and executed.
261     * @param parent    The parent component for displaying error messages in dialog boxes.
262     */
263    private static void launchApp(String jarPrefix, Component parent) {
264        List<File> jarDirs = new ArrayList<>();
265        File ownDir = ownJarDirectory();
266        if (ownDir != null) {
267            jarDirs.add(ownDir);
268        }
269        jarDirs.add(new File(System.getProperty("user.dir"), JAR_DIR));
270
271        File jarFile = null;
272        for (File jarDir : jarDirs) {
273            File[] matches = jarDir.listFiles(f -> f.getName().startsWith(jarPrefix) && f.getName().endsWith(".jar"));
274            if (matches != null && matches.length > 0) {
275                jarFile = matches[0];
276                break;
277            }
278        }
279
280        if (jarFile == null) {
281            StringBuilder searched = new StringBuilder();
282            for (File jarDir : jarDirs) {
283                searched.append('\n').append(jarDir.getAbsolutePath());
284            }
285            JOptionPane.showMessageDialog(parent,
286                                          "No matching JAR found for prefix:\n" + jarPrefix
287                                                  + "\n\nSearched in:" + searched,
288                                          "Error", JOptionPane.ERROR_MESSAGE);
289            return;
290        }
291
292        try {
293            new ProcessBuilder(javaExecutable(), "-jar", jarFile.getAbsolutePath())
294                    .inheritIO()
295                    .start();
296        } catch (IOException e) {
297            JOptionPane.showMessageDialog(parent,
298                                          "Failed to launch:\n" + jarFile.getName() + "\n\n" + e.getMessage(),
299                                          "Error", JOptionPane.ERROR_MESSAGE);
300        }
301    }
302
303    /**
304     * Returns the folder that holds the JAR (or classes folder) this class was loaded from,
305     * or {@code null} if it cannot be determined.
306     */
307    private static File ownJarDirectory() {
308        try {
309            Path location = Path.of(PaintLauncher.class.getProtectionDomain().getCodeSource().getLocation().toURI());
310            Path parent   = location.getParent();
311            return parent == null ? null : parent.toFile();
312        } catch (Exception e) {
313            return null;
314        }
315    }
316
317    /**
318     * Returns the java executable of the Java the launcher itself runs on, so the applications
319     * start on the same Java (in the bundled app: its built-in Java). On Windows {@code javaw.exe}
320     * is preferred, so no console window opens. Falls back to {@code java} on the PATH.
321     */
322    private static String javaExecutable() {
323        boolean windows = System.getProperty("os.name", "").toLowerCase(Locale.ROOT).startsWith("windows");
324        Path    bin     = Path.of(System.getProperty("java.home"), "bin");
325        String[] names  = windows ? new String[]{"javaw.exe", "java.exe"} : new String[]{"java"};
326        for (String name : names) {
327            Path candidate = bin.resolve(name);
328            if (Files.isExecutable(candidate)) {
329                return candidate.toString();
330            }
331        }
332        return "java";
333    }
334
335    public static void main(String[] args) {
336        SwingUtilities.invokeLater(PaintLauncher::createAndShowGUI);
337    }
338}
